title: Descent data on affine morphisms are effective for an fpqc covering $\{X\to S\}$ (Stacks 0245)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] such that the one-member family $\{f:X\to S\}$ is an fpqc covering of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Let $V\to X$ be an affine morphism [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and let $\varphi$ be a descent datum on $V$ over $X/S$ [def-pd-descent-datum]: an isomorphism $\varphi:\mathrm{pr}_0^*V\to\mathrm{pr}_1^*V$ of schemes over $X_2=X\times_SX$ [def-pc-fibre-product], where $\mathrm{pr}_0,\mathrm{pr}_1:X_2\to X$ are the projections, satisfying $\mathrm{pr}_{02}^*\varphi=\mathrm{pr}_{12}^*\varphi\circ\mathrm{pr}_{01}^*\varphi$ over $X\times_SX\times_SX$. Then $(V,\varphi)$ is effective: there are a scheme $U$ with a morphism $U\to S$ and an isomorphism $\psi:U\times_SX\to V$ of schemes over $X$ such that $\varphi\circ\mathrm{pr}_0^*\psi=\mathrm{pr}_1^*\psi\circ\mathrm{can}_U$, where $\mathrm{can}_U:\mathrm{pr}_0^*(U\times_SX)\to\mathrm{pr}_1^*(U\times_SX)$ is the composite of the canonical isomorphisms of both sides with $U\times_SX_2$.

proof.text: *Step 1 (affine morphisms are stable under base change: hypothesis (1) of [lem-galois-fpqc-descending-types-morphisms] for $\mathcal P$ = affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]).* If $Y\to V$ is affine and $V'\to V$ is any morphism of schemes, then $Y\times_VV'\to V'$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (1). (Source: 'Being affine is a property of morphisms of schemes which is ... preserved under any base change, see Morphisms, Lemma 01SD'.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0245, proof, first sentence (Morphisms Tag 01SD, morphisms-lemma-base-change-affine)

proof.text: *Step 2 (finite coproducts of affine morphisms are affine: hypothesis (2)).* Let $h_j:Y_j\to V_j$ ($j=1,\dots,m$) be affine, and let $Y=\coprod_jY_j$, $V=\coprod_jV_j$ with coprojections $\iota'_j:Y_j\to Y$, $\iota_j:V_j\to V$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]: open immersions with pairwise disjoint images covering $Y$, resp. $V$. Let $h:Y\to V$ be the induced morphism, $h\circ\iota'_j=\iota_j\circ h_j$; then $h^{-1}(\iota_j(V_j))=\iota'_j(Y_j)$ (a point $\iota'_k(y)$ maps to $\iota_k(h_k(y))$, which lies in $\iota_j(V_j)$ only for $k=j$). Let $W\subseteq V$ be an affine open [pqf-def-affine-morphism]; we show $h^{-1}(W)$ is affine. Put $W_j=W\cap\iota_j(V_j)$: open, and closed in $W$, its complement in $W$ being $W\cap\bigcup_{k\ne j}\iota_k(V_k)$. Under an isomorphism $W\cong\operatorname{Spec}R_W$ [def-pc-scheme], $W_j=D(e_j)$ for an idempotent $e_j\in R_W$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent], which is the image of the open immersion $\operatorname{Spec}(R_W)_{e_j}\to W$ [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion]; so $W_j$ is an affine open of $V$, and $\iota_j^{-1}(W_j)$ is an affine open of $V_j$ ($\iota_j$ is an isomorphism onto its open image). Since $h_j$ is affine, $h_j^{-1}(\iota_j^{-1}(W_j))$ is affine, hence so is its isomorphic image $\iota'_j(h_j^{-1}(\iota_j^{-1}(W_j)))=h^{-1}(W_j)$. Thus the open subscheme $h^{-1}(W)$ is covered by the finitely many pairwise disjoint affine opens $h^{-1}(W_1),\dots,h^{-1}(W_m)$; it is therefore their coproduct (morphisms out of the pieces glue uniquely, the overlaps being empty), and a finite disjoint union of affine schemes is affine [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (4). Hence $h$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. (Source: 'Being affine is a property of morphisms of schemes which is local on the base, see Morphisms, Lemma 01S8'; the locality on the base is used here only for the decomposition of $W$ into the clopen pieces $W_j$.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0245, proof, first sentence (Morphisms Tag 01S8, morphisms-lemma-characterize-affine), applied to hypothesis (2) of Lemma Tag 02W3

proof.text: *Step 3 (hypothesis (3), set-up: rings).* Let $X\to S$ be a flat surjective morphism of affine schemes and $(V,\varphi)$ a descent datum over $X/S$ [def-pd-descent-datum] with $V\to X$ affine. Choose isomorphisms $X\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$, $S\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-pc-scheme]; transporting $X\to S$, $V\to X$, $\varphi$ and the sought $U,\psi$ along them (the fibre products over isomorphic bases are canonically isomorphic [def-pc-fibre-product]) we may assume $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Then $X\to S$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a unique ring map $R\to A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], which is flat since $X\to S$ is [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. As $V\to X$ is affine and $X$ is affine, $V$ is affine [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (2); so (again up to an isomorphism) $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $V\to X$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a ring map $A\to B$, making $B$ an $A$-algebra [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. (Surjectivity of $X\to S$, i.e. faithful flatness of $R\to A$, is not needed below.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0245, proof: 'Say X = Spec(A) and S = Spec(R) so that R -> A is a faithfully flat ring map ... V = Spec(B) for some A-algebra B (Morphisms, Definition 01S6)'

proof.text: *Step 4 (the descent datum in rings).* All tensor products are over $R$; for commutative $R$-algebras they are the rings of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], whose universal property (2),(3) gives the associativity and symmetry isomorphisms used tacitly, e.g. $B\otimes_A(A\otimes A)\cong B\otimes A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] (applied twice for the triple products) $X_2=X\times_SX=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes A)$ with $\mathrm{pr}_0,\mathrm{pr}_1$ the spectra of $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, $a\mapsto1\otimes a$; $\mathrm{pr}_0^*V=V\times_{X,\mathrm{pr}_0}X_2=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes A)$ and $\mathrm{pr}_1^*V=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes B)$ as schemes over $X_2$ ($A\otimes A$ acting factorwise); $X_3=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes A\otimes A)$, and the pullbacks along $\mathrm{pr}_{01},\mathrm{pr}_{12},\mathrm{pr}_{02}$ of $\mathrm{pr}_0^*V$ and $\mathrm{pr}_1^*V$ are the spectra of $B\otimes A\otimes A$, $A\otimes B\otimes A$, $A\otimes A\otimes B$ (the factor $B$ in the slot of the corresponding projection). Morphisms between spectra are the spectra of unique ring maps, contravariantly [def-weil-affine-spectrum], so $\varphi=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi^\sharp)$ for an isomorphism of $A\otimes A$-algebras $\varphi^\sharp:A\otimes B\to B\otimes A$. Put $\theta=(\varphi^\sharp)^{-1}:B\otimes A\to A\otimes B$, an isomorphism of $A\otimes A$-algebras. Then $\mathrm{pr}_{01}^*\varphi$, $\mathrm{pr}_{12}^*\varphi$, $\mathrm{pr}_{02}^*\varphi$ are the spectra of the inverses of $\theta_{01}=\theta\otimes\mathrm{id}_A:B\otimes A\otimes A\to A\otimes B\otimes A$, $\theta_{12}=\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\theta:A\otimes B\otimes A\to A\otimes A\otimes B$ and $\theta_{02}:B\otimes A\otimes A\to A\otimes A\otimes B$, $b\otimes a\otimes a'\mapsto\sum_kx_k\otimes a\otimes y_k$ where $\theta(b\otimes a')=\sum_kx_k\otimes y_k$ ($\theta$ acting on the slots $0,2$). By contravariance the cocycle condition $\mathrm{pr}_{02}^*\varphi=\mathrm{pr}_{12}^*\varphi\circ\mathrm{pr}_{01}^*\varphi$ of [def-pd-descent-datum] becomes $\theta_{02}^{-1}=\theta_{01}^{-1}\circ\theta_{12}^{-1}$, i.e. $\theta_{02}=\theta_{12}\circ\theta_{01}$. (This is the source's 'Inverting these arrows we see that we have a descent datum for modules with respect to $R\to A$ as in Definition 023G'.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0245, proof: 'The isomorphism phi corresponds to an isomorphism of rings phi^#: B (x)_R A <- A (x)_R B as A (x)_R A-algebras. The cocycle condition ... Inverting these arrows ... descent datum for modules ... Definition 023G' (definition-descent-datum-modules, line 271)

proof.text: *Step 5 (the coaction $\delta$; counit and coassociativity).* Define $\delta:B\to A\otimes B$, $\delta(b)=\theta(b\otimes1)$. It is a ring map (composite of $b\mapsto b\otimes1$ and $\theta$), and $A$-linear for the left $A$-structure of $A\otimes B$: $\delta(ab)=\theta((a\otimes1)\cdot(b\otimes1))=(a\otimes1)\theta(b\otimes1)$ by $A\otimes A$-linearity of $\theta$; so $\delta$ is a homomorphism of $A$-algebras. *Coassociativity.* Write $\delta(b)=\sum_kx_k\otimes y_k$. Evaluate $\theta_{02}=\theta_{12}\circ\theta_{01}$ (Step 4) at $b\otimes1\otimes1$: the left side is $\sum_kx_k\otimes1\otimes y_k=(\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\iota)(\delta(b))$; the right side is $\theta_{12}(\sum_kx_k\otimes y_k\otimes1)=\sum_kx_k\otimes\theta(y_k\otimes1)=(\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\delta)(\delta(b))$, under $A\otimes(A\otimes B)=A\otimes A\otimes B$. *Counit* (the source's remark after Definition 023V that $\Delta^*\varphi=\mathrm{id}$, written out). Let $m:A\otimes A\otimes A\to A$ be the multiplication and tensor each of $\theta_{01},\theta_{12},\theta_{02}$ (maps of $A\otimes A\otimes A$-modules) with $A$ over $A\otimes A\otimes A$ via $m$; the three modules $B\otimes A\otimes A$, $A\otimes B\otimes A$, $A\otimes A\otimes B$ become $B$ (e.g. $b\otimes a\otimes a'\mapsto aa'b$). Tracing $b\mapsto b\otimes1\otimes1$ (resp. $1\otimes b\otimes1$) through the definitions, each of the three becomes the same map $\varepsilon:B\to B$, $\varepsilon(b)=\mu(\delta(b))$ with $\mu(a\otimes b)=ab$; and each is bijective, being the base change of an isomorphism. Hence $\varepsilon=\varepsilon\circ\varepsilon$ with $\varepsilon$ bijective, so $\varepsilon=\mathrm{id}_B$, i.e. $\mu(\delta(b))=b$ for all $b$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0245, proof (the cocycle diagram, lines 9180-9188); Definition Tag 023V and the paragraph after it (line 8136: 'In fact, Delta^* phi is equal to the identity. This is a good exercise'), written out here

proof.text: *Step 6 (descending the algebra).* By Steps 3 and 5, $R\to A$ is flat and $\delta:B\to A\otimes B$ is a homomorphism of $A$-algebras satisfying the counit and coassociativity conditions of [lem-galois-flat-algebra-descent]. That node gives the $R$-subalgebra $C=\{b\in B:\delta(b)=1\otimes b\}=\{b\in B:\theta(b\otimes1)=1\otimes b\}$ of $B$ and the isomorphism of $A$-algebras $\kappa:A\otimes C\to B$, $a\otimes c\mapsto ac$. (The source: 'apply Proposition 023N to obtain an $R$-module $C=\mathrm{Ker}(B\to A\otimes_RB)$ and an isomorphism $A\otimes_RC\cong B$ ... the product $cc'$ lies in $C$ since $\varphi$ is an algebra homomorphism'.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0245, proof, lines 9192-9200 (Proposition Tag 023N, proposition-descent-module)

proof.text: *Step 7 (the descended scheme and the compatibility).* Put $U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $U\to S$ the spectrum of $R\to C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $U\times_SX=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes C)$ (up to the symmetry isomorphism) over $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $U\times_SX_2=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes A\otimes C)$, through which $\mathrm{can}_U$ factors. Let $\psi=\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa^{-1}):U\times_SX\to V$; it is an isomorphism of schemes over $X$ since $\kappa$ is an isomorphism of $A$-algebras [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Identify $\mathrm{pr}_0^*(U\times_SX)$ and $\mathrm{pr}_1^*(U\times_SX)$ with $U\times_SX_2$ by the canonical isomorphisms, so that $\mathrm{can}_U$ becomes the identity; then $\mathrm{pr}_0^*\psi$ and $\mathrm{pr}_1^*\psi$ are the spectra of the $A\otimes A$-algebra maps $\beta_0:B\otimes A\to A\otimes A\otimes C$, $b\otimes a'\mapsto(1\otimes a'\otimes1)\cdot\kappa^{-1}(b)_{02}$, and $\beta_1:A\otimes B\to A\otimes A\otimes C$, $a\otimes b\mapsto(a\otimes1\otimes1)\cdot\kappa^{-1}(b)_{12}$ (with $(\,)_{02}$, $(\,)_{12}$ placing $A\otimes C$ in the slots $0,2$, resp. $1,2$). The required identity $\varphi\circ\mathrm{pr}_0^*\psi=\mathrm{pr}_1^*\psi\circ\mathrm{can}_U$ is, by contravariance [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\beta_0\circ\varphi^\sharp=\beta_1$, i.e. $\beta_0=\beta_1\circ\theta$. Both sides are $A\otimes A$-algebra maps $B\otimes A\to A\otimes A\otimes C$, and $B\otimes A$ is generated as an $A\otimes A$-module by the elements $c\otimes1$, $c\in C$ (as $\kappa$ is surjective, every $b$ is $\sum_ia_ic_i$, and $b\otimes a'=\sum_i(a_i\otimes a')(c_i\otimes1)$). On these, $\beta_0(c\otimes1)=1\otimes1\otimes c$ because $\kappa^{-1}(c)=1\otimes c$, and $\beta_1(\theta(c\otimes1))=\beta_1(\delta(c))=\beta_1(1\otimes c)=1\otimes1\otimes c$ because $c\in C$. Hence $\beta_0=\beta_1\circ\theta$, and $(V,\varphi)$ is effective. This verifies hypothesis (3) of [lem-galois-fpqc-descending-types-morphisms] for $\mathcal P$ = affine. (Source: 'Hence C is an R-algebra whose base change to A is isomorphic to B compatibly with descent data. Applying Spec we obtain a scheme U over S such that $(V,\varphi)\cong(X\times_SU,can)$'.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0245, proof, last two sentences (lines 9200-9204)

proof.text: *Step 8 (conclusion).* By Steps 1, 2 and 3-7, the property $\mathcal P$ = 'affine' [pqf-def-affine-morphism] satisfies hypotheses (1), (2), (3) of [lem-galois-fpqc-descending-types-morphisms]. Applying it to the fpqc covering $\{f:X\to S\}$ and to the descent datum $(V,\varphi)$ with $V\to X$ affine gives $U\to S$ and $\psi:U\times_SX\to V$ over $X$ with $\varphi\circ\mathrm{pr}_0^*\psi=\mathrm{pr}_1^*\psi\circ\mathrm{can}_U$, which is the statement. (Source: 'Hence Lemma 02W3 applies and it suffices to prove the statement of the lemma in case the fpqc-covering is given by a single {X -> S} flat surjective morphism of affines.')
